title: Construction Logbook and Completion Dossier for Houses 2026
desc: Who keeps the construction logbook and as-built drawings? What a house completion dossier contains and how long it is kept, with 2026 fines.
summary: Responsibility for the construction logbook, as-built drawings and completion dossier under the Construction Law 2025 and Decree 207/2026/ND-CP, and the papers homeowners should keep.
body: p

Once the house is built, the paperwork matters as much as the bricks: when registering the house in the land certificate, repairing, claiming warranty or reselling, the owner needs the project dossier. This article summarises the rules on the construction logbook, as-built drawings and completion dossier under the Construction Law 2025 and Decree 207/2026/ND-CP.
h2
1. The construction logbook: who keeps it?
p

Under Clause 13, Article 15 of Decree 207/2026/ND-CP, the construction contractor is responsible for keeping the construction logbook and the as-built drawings in accordance with Appendix II of the Decree. The contractor must also prepare and store construction management records for the work it performs, and quality management records must match the actual time of performance on site (Clauses 8 and 17, Article 15).
p
The logbook records daily progress: work done, materials brought in, incidents and the homeowner's requests. When a dispute arises over quality, schedule or variations, it is important evidence.
h2
2. What are as-built drawings?
p

As-built drawings (bản vẽ hoàn công) are drawings of the completed work showing the actual position, dimensions, materials and equipment used (Clause 3, Article 2). The construction contractor prepares them and takes part in acceptance (Point h, Clause 2, Article 61 of the Construction Law 2025). Before handover, the contractor must give the project owner the as-built drawings, operating instructions, maintenance procedures, and a list of equipment and spare materials (Clause 3, Article 58).
h2
3. The completion dossier
p
The completion dossier is the set of records and documents relating to the construction investment process that must be kept when the work is put into use (Clause 4, Article 2). Under Article 28:
ul

The project owner organises its preparation after completion acceptance, in line with Appendix VII of Decree 207/2026/ND-CP, and is responsible for its accuracy and truthfulness; each contractor is responsible for the part it prepares.
It is prepared in Vietnamese.
The project owner keeps one set, as originals and electronic copies; where no original exists, a certified true copy or lawful copy is used.
p

For detached houses of fewer than 7 floors (and no more than 1 basement), preparing and storing the dossier under the Decree is encouraged; houses of 7 floors or more, or 2 or more basements, must comply (Clause 3, Article 10).
h2
4. Which documents should the homeowner keep?
ol
The construction permit and the approved drawings attached to it (if a permit was required).
Design records, and the design, construction and supervision contracts.
Quality certificates and conformity certificates for materials and equipment; material acceptance records (Clause 7, Article 14).
The construction logbook, and acceptance records for individual tasks, stages and final completion.
As-built drawings, maintenance procedures and equipment warranty documents.
p

Records serving the management and use of the work are kept for at least the service life of the work (Clause 2, Article 42 of the Construction Law 2025). For registering the house in the red book, see As-built Completion and Registering a House in the Red Book.
h2
5. Related fines
p
Under Article 23 and Article 22 of Decree 339/2026/ND-CP (levels for organisations; individuals pay half under Clause 4, Article 5):
ul
A contractor without a construction logbook, or one kept improperly: VND 10–20 million, and must keep the logbook.
A contractor that does not prepare as-built drawings or prepares them improperly: VND 40–60 million, and must redo them.
Quality management records not matching the actual time: VND 60–80 million.
A project owner that does not organise the preparation of the completion dossier as required: VND 60–80 million.
note

This article is a summary for reference only and does not replace the legal texts. The logbook form (Appendix II) and the list of completion records (Appendix VII) of Decree 207/2026/ND-CP are not yet in our library; cross-check the original on the National Legal Portal.
